blocking.where: showcase.json key_facts ("Dive Centre Manly operating since: 1962"); showcase.json spike_explainer ("Dive Centre Manly has served the local community from Belgrave Street since 1962"); history.mdx ("Diving itself became a fixture of the local economy in 1962, when Dive Centre Manly opened on Belgrave Street. It has served the Manly community from that address ever since"); composition.json timeline ("1962: Dive Centre Manly opens")
blocking.claim: A business called Dive Centre Manly opened on Belgrave Street in 1962 and has continuously served the community under that name/identity ever since.
blocking.problem: The sheet's own source (History Matters, Nov 2024) is a simplified secondary account; the actual current operator's own history page contradicts the continuity implied here. Fetched live: divecentremanly.com.au now permanently redirects to divesydney.com.au (10 Belgrave Street, Manly) — the current owner-facing tagline reads 'Keeping Our Heads Below Water Since 1993,' not 1962. Their own /about-us history page states the address opened in 1962 as 'Ron Harding's Sports Store' (one of only three dive stores in Sydney at the time); it was only later, under owners Richard and Janet from 1993, that it operated as 'Dive Centre Manly' for the next 30 years; the current owner Michael took over in 2023 and now trades as Dive Sydney. So: (a) the business open in 1962 was not named or operating as "Dive Centre Manly" — that name dates to the 1993 ownership change — and (b) the business no longer trades under the name "Dive Centre Manly" at all as of 2023, a fact the page nowhere discloses.
blocking.evidence: https://divesydney.com.au/ (redirect target of divecentremanly.com.au; homepage tagline 'Keeping Our Heads Below Water Since 1993', address 10 Belgrave Street, Manly NSW 2095); https://divesydney.com.au/about-us/ (history: 1962 'Ron Harding's Sports Store' -> renamed/operated as 'Dive Centre Manly' under Richard & Janet from 1993 -> current owner Michael since 2023, now trading as Dive Sydney)
blocking.fix: Reword to preserve the true continuity (a dive shop has operated at this Belgrave Street address continuously since 1962) without asserting the name "Dive Centre Manly" existed then or exists now. Suggested wording: timeline title 'Dive shop opens on Belgrave Street'; description 'A dive shop (Ron Harding's Sports Store, one of only three in Sydney at the time) begins operating from Belgrave Street; it later traded as Dive Centre Manly and, since 2023, as Dive Sydney.' key_facts row -> label 'Dive shop operating since', value '1962 (now trading as Dive Sydney)'. history.mdx -> 'Diving itself became a fixture of the local economy in 1962, when a dive shop opened on Belgrave Street. Under different names and owners — Dive Centre Manly from 1993, Dive Sydney since 2023 — a dive business has served the Manly community from that address ever since.'

advisory.where: history.mdx, opening paragraph ("Twice in less than forty years, and then again in the 1920s, the public's access to this small cove at Manly was contested...")
advisory.claim: Implies three distinct access-contest episodes (twice, plus 'again' in the 1920s).
advisory.problem: The ledger only supports two contested-access episodes: the 1885 exclusion (resolved 1898, F51) and the 1920s amusement-park scheme (F30/F31). The 1920s scheme appears to be the second half of the 'twice' and then gets re-named as a third, separate 'again' event, which reads as inflating the count. Not a factual fabrication (no invented event), just confusing/ambiguous phrasing that a careful reader could misread as claiming an extra dispute.
advisory.evidence: research/<slug>.json F51 (1885/1898 exclusion-and-return) and F30/F31 (1920s amusement-park fight) are the only two access-contest events in the fact sheet.
advisory.fix: Reword to 'Twice in the space of about forty years — first by private exclusion, then by a 1920s redevelopment scheme — the public's access to this small cove at Manly was contested, before the state itself eventually chose to protect the water rather than develop it.'
